extracted.intended_audience: undergraduate or beginning graduate students learning abstract algebra (group theory, modules, PIDs, and introductory representation theory)
extracted.subtask_description: Expository textbook material covering Sylow-theory consequences, composition series and Jordan–Hölder, the structure theorem for finitely generated abelian groups (via PID/module theory and Smith normal form), and introductory representation theory of algebras.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orbits of a p-group action have p-power sizes
rubrics_metrics.description: Because P is a p-group, the orbits of the action have sizes which are in {p^0, p^1, p^2, ... }.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used when P acts on a set (e.g., Sylow p-subgroups by conjugation): orbit sizes are powers of p, so counting orbits modulo p gives information about fixed points (used to deduce congruences like np ≡ 1 (mod p)).

rubrics_metrics.name: P is the only fixed point of conjugation action on Sylow p-subgroups
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim: when P acts on the set S of Sylow p-subgroups by conjugation, P is the only fixed point of this action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Q is a fixed point (xQx^{-1}=Q for all x∈P), then P and Q lie in the normalizer N_G(Q); applying Sylow-step (Step 2) within N_G(Q) shows P and Q are conjugate in N_G(Q), hence equal. This is used to count fixed points.

rubrics_metrics.name: np ≡ 1 (mod p) for number of Sylow p-subgroups
rubrics_metrics.description: From the action of P on the set S of Sylow p-subgroups and the fixed-point count, np ≡ 1 (mod p).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine the fact that orbit sizes are p-powers with there being exactly one fixed point (P) to obtain the congruence; this is a standard Sylow-theory congruence used in classifying Sylow p-subgroups.

rubrics_metrics.name: np divides |G| (number of Sylow p-subgroups divides group order)
rubrics_metrics.description: Since the action of G on its Sylow p-subgroups by conjugation has one orbit (Step 2), the orbit-stabilizer theorem implies np divides |G|.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in final Sylow conclusions: with np ≡ 1 (mod p) and np | |G|, one gets restrictions on possible numbers of Sylow p-subgroups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: simple group
rubrics_metrics.description: A simple group is a group with no normal subgroups other than itself and the trivial group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Basic notion: composition factors of composition series are simple groups; classification of finite simple groups is a central objective in group theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: composition series
rubrics_metrics.description: A composition series of a group G is a sequence of subgroups H0, H1, ..., Hn such that {1}=H0 ⊴ H1 ⊴ ... ⊴ Hn=G of maximal length (i.e. n as large as possible, with all Hi distinct). The composition factors are H1/H0, H2/H1, ..., Hn/Hn−1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maximality implies the composition factors are all simple groups; two composition series are considered equivalent if they have the same composition factors up to permutation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jordan–Hölder theorem
rubrics_metrics.description: Every finite group G admits a unique composition series up to equivalence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uniqueness here means the multiset of composition factors (simple groups), up to permutation, is invariant; analogous to uniqueness of prime factorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification categories for finite simple groups (overview)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every finite simple group falls into one of: Z/pZ for p prime; the alternating groups A_n for n ≥ 5; simple groups of Lie type; or one of twenty-six sporadic groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a high-level taxonomy (no proofs here); names and examples (baby monster, monster) and orders are given to illustrate the oddity and scale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: finitely generated abelian group
rubrics_metrics.description: An abelian group G is finitely generated if it is finitely generated as a Z-module (there exist b1,...,bm ∈ G such that every x ∈ G is c1 b1 + ... + cm bm for some integers ci).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This viewpoint treats abelian groups as Z-modules and sets up the structure theorem context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fundamental theorem of finitely generated abelian groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Let G be a finitely generated abelian group. Then there exists an integer r and prime powers q1,...,qm (not necessarily distinct) such that G ≅ Z^r ⊕ Z/q1Z ⊕ ... ⊕ Z/qmZ. This decomposition is unique up to permutation of the Z/qiZ summands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States classification into free part Z^r and finite torsion part expressed as cyclic prime-power factors; underlies many classification results and is a corollary of the general PID structure theorem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: rank of a finitely generated abelian group
rubrics_metrics.description: The rank of a finitely generated abelian group G is the integer r in the decomposition G ≅ Z^r ⊕ (torsion part).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counts the free (infinite cyclic) summands; intrinsic invariant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: prime element in a UFD
rubrics_metrics.description: If R is a UFD, then p ∈ R is a prime element if (p) is a prime ideal and p ≠ 0. Equivalently in a UFD, p is prime iff whenever p = xy, either x or y is a unit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generalizes integer primes to unique-factorization domains; used in factorization statements in structure theorems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: divisibility r | s
rubrics_metrics.description: We say r divides s if s = r′ r for some r′ ∈ R (written r | s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In UFDs this corresponds to exponent-wise inequalities of prime factorizations; basic notion used throughout module/ideal factorization arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition: PIDs are Noetherian UFDs
rubrics_metrics.description: If R is a PID, then it is Noetherian and also a UFD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof sketch: Noetherian is obvious for PIDs; UFD property uses principal-ness of (a,b) to extract gcds and imitate the Z proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chinese remainder theorem for rings
rubrics_metrics.description: Let m and n be relatively prime elements (i.e., (m)+(n)=(1)). Then R/(mn) ≅ R/(m) × R/(n).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct explicit map R/(m) × R/(n) → R/(mn) via linear combination r·bn + s·am where am+bn=1; used to split modules/rings when factors are coprime.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Noetherian R-module (two equivalent conditions)
rubrics_metrics.description: An R-module M is Noetherian iff (a) its submodules satisfy the ascending chain condition (no infinite strictly increasing chain), or (b) every submodule of M is finitely generated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalence mirrors Noetherian rings; important hypothesis in proofs (e.g., kernels in finite-generation arguments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure theorem for finitely generated modules over a PID (invariant form)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let R be a PID and M a finitely generated R-module. Then M ≅ ⊕_{i=1}^m R/(s_i) for some s_i (possibly zero) satisfying s_1 | s_2 | ... | s_m.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This invariant-factor decomposition is the primary statement; uniqueness up to units and order; yields the primary (prime-power) form by factoring s_i.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure theorem (primary form / corollary)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let R be a PID and M a finitely generated R-module. Then M ≅ R^r ⊕ R/(q1) ⊕ ... ⊕ R/(qm) where each q_i is a prime power p_i^{e_i}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalently describes module as free part plus direct sum of primary cyclic modules; follows by factoring invariant factors and applying Chinese remainder theorem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remark: uniqueness up to permutation of summands
rubrics_metrics.description: In both the invariant and primary forms the decomposition is unique up to permutation of the summands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The subsequent subsections (uniqueness proofs) show how intrinsic invariants (like dimensions of successive peM/pe+1M) determine the decomposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: free R-module
rubrics_metrics.description: A free R-module is a module of the form R^n (or more generally ⊕_I R for an indexing set I), i.e., it has a basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to reduce finitely generated module problems to linear-algebra-style problems on free modules and matrices over R.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma: direct sum of Noetherian modules is Noetherian
rubrics_metrics.description: If M and N are Noetherian R-modules, then M ⊕ N is Noetherian.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof constructs projections and generators for appropriate submodules; used to show kernels in finitely-generated-module surjections are finitely generated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniqueness of free module's rank
rubrics_metrics.description: For a commutative integral domain R, if a free module M has a finite basis, then every other basis has the same number of elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof passes to fraction field F of R and applies dimension theorem for vector spaces; fundamental invariant of free modules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniqueness of exponents in torsion decomposition (for R/(p^{e_i}))
rubrics_metrics.description: Let R be a PID, p a prime element, and M ≅ ⊕_{i=1}^m R/(p^{e_i}). Then the e_i are unique up to permutation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Idea: intrinsic invariants peM/pe+1M (which are R/(p)-vector spaces) and their dimensions determine the multiset of e_i; example and counting of successive quotients show how exponents appear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: rM (multiplication-by-r submodule)
rubrics_metrics.description: For r ∈ R and an R-module M, define rM = {r m | m ∈ M}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to form the successive submodules peM and their quotients peM/pe+1M as intrinsic invariants to detect primary decomposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma: peM/pe+1M is an R/(p)-vector space
rubrics_metrics.description: For each integer e ≥ 0, peM/pe+1M is a vector space over R/(p).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thus one can take dimensions (finite or infinite) of these quotients to recover multiplicities of prime-power summands in the decomposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniqueness of full decomposition (free + primary parts)
rubrics_metrics.description: If M ≅ R^r ⊕ ⊕_{i=1}^m R/(q_i), then the integer r and the prime powers q_i are unique up to permutation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tor(M) (torsion submodule) equals the summand with R^r-component zero and is intrinsic; M/Tor(M) ≅ R^r determines r; combine with primary-case uniqueness to conclude full uniqueness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Smith normal form (SNF) theorem
rubrics_metrics.description: Let R be a PID, M = R^m, N = R^n, and T: M → N a linear map. Set k = min{m,n}. One can choose bases so that T has diagonal entries s1,...,sk with s1 | s2 | ... | s_k and all off-diagonal entries zero (padding with zero rows/columns as needed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SNF reduces classification of finitely generated modules (as cokernels of T) to diagonal form; proving SNF uses gcd-based Euclidean-type row/column operations permitted over a PID.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted basis changes / elementary operations for SNF
rubrics_metrics.description: Allowed operations include swapping rows/columns, adding a multiple of one column to another, adding a multiple of one row to another, and more generally left-/right-multiplying by invertible matrices (changes of basis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These operations correspond to changing bases of source and target free modules and are the tools used to bring a matrix into Smith normal form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim: 'Euclidean algorithm' on two entries via base changes
rubrics_metrics.description: If a and b are entries in the same row or column, one can change bases to replace a by gcd(a,b) and b by something else.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct linear combinations using coefficients x,y with gcd(a,b)=x a + y b and use invertible 2×2 matrices to realize the replacement; iterating this isolates gcds to produce SNF.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: associative k-algebra (with 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: A k-algebra A is a (possibly noncommutative) ring equipped with a ring homomorphism k → A whose image is the 'copy of k' (so λ·a = a·λ for λ∈k and a∈A). Equivalently, a k-vector space with an associative bilinear multiplication and identity 1_A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets the ambient algebraic object whose representations (left modules) will be studied; remarks note some authors omit associativity or 1 but that is not needed here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example / construction: group algebra k[G]
rubrics_metrics.description: k[G] is the k-vector space with basis indexed by elements of a group G and multiplication extending group multiplication linearly (e.g., k[Z/2Z] = {a·1_G + b·x} with explicit product).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Representations of k[G] correspond to group representations of G (homomorphisms G → GL(V)); k[G] is a central example linking group and algebra representation theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: homomorphism of k-algebras
rubrics_metrics.description: A homomorphism T: A → B of k-algebras is a linear map respecting multiplication (T(xy)=T(x)T(y)) and sending 1_A to 1_B; it's both a ring and vector-space homomorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to define representations as algebra homomorphisms into matrix algebras and to discuss algebra morphisms in constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: direct sum of k-algebras A ⊕ B
rubrics_metrics.description: Given k-algebras A and B, the direct sum A ⊕ B consists of pairs (a,b) with addition componentwise and multiplication (a,b)(a',b')=(aa',bb'). (Alternate phrasing in text declares ab=0 for a∈A,b∈B in a notation a+b.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This product algebra has identity (1_A,1_B); representations of A⊕B split into representations of A and B (see proposition).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: representation of a k-algebra (left A-module)
rubrics_metrics.description: A representation of a k-algebra A is a k-vector space V together with an action · of A on V satisfying (a+b)·v = a·v + b·v, a·(v+w) = a·v + a·w, (ab)·v = a·(b·v), and λ·v = λ v for λ∈k (in particular 1_A·v=v).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalently a k-algebra homomorphism ρ: A → Mat(V). Representations are often abbreviated by V when ρ is understood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation as algebra homomorphism ρ: A → Mat(V)
rubrics_metrics.description: The action of A on V is equivalent to giving a k-algebra homomorphism ρ: A → Mat(V), with a·v defined as ρ(a)(v).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This perspective yields concrete matrix realizations of abstract algebra elements and facilitates linear-algebraic manipulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regular representation Reg(A)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any k-algebra A is naturally a representation over itself with action a·b = ab; this is the regular representation, denoted Reg(A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Important canonical example: A acts on itself by left multiplication; often used to analyze decomposition into irreducibles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct sum of representations
rubrics_metrics.description: If V=(V,ρ_V) and W=(W,ρ_W) are representations of A, then V ⊕ W is a representation with action a·(v,w) = (a·v, a·w).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes how composite representations are formed; matrix of ρ(a) on V⊕W is block-diagonal with ρ_V(a) and ρ_W(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition: representations of A ⊕ B are VA ⊕ VB
rubrics_metrics.description: Every representation of A ⊕ B is of the form V_A ⊕ V_B where V_A is a representation of A and V_B a representation of B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sketch: use idempotent projections ρ(1_A) and ρ(1_B) to split V into VA and VB; actions of A and B act trivially on the other component respectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: subrepresentation
rubrics_metrics.description: A subrepresentation W ⊆ V is a subspace invariant under the action of A: for all a∈A and w∈W, a·w ∈ W.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analogous to invariant subspaces in linear algebra; subrepresentations are the building blocks for decomposition questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: irreducible and indecomposable representations
rubrics_metrics.description: An irreducible (or irreducible representation) has no proper nonzero subrepresentations. An indecomposable representation cannot be written as a direct sum V = W1 ⊕ W2 of two proper subrepresentations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Irreducibles are the atomic building blocks for semisimple representation theory; indecomposable is a weaker notion relevant when complete reducibility fails.
